candidate_nodes.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_setup
candidate_nodes.remark: The source says such phi exist by the theory of SL2-triples but are not unique.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Definition extracted from the introductory definition of degenerate Whittaker data; OCR normalized phi, theta_f, and U'' notation.
candidate_nodes.statement: Given a nilpotent orbit O in g and f in O, choose a one-parameter subgroup phi: F^* -> G satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f for all s in F^*. Define U, respectively U', as the unipotent subgroup whose Lie algebra consists of those X such that lim_{s->0} phi(s).X = 0, respectively lim_{s->0} phi(s)s^-1.X = 0. Define U'' as the subgroup of U generated by U' and the stabilizer of f in U. The function gamma |-> psi(tr(f log gamma)) is a character of U'', denoted theta_f.

candidate_nodes.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_forms
candidate_nodes.remark: The exact Hom notation and acting group should be checked against the PDF before admission.
candidate_nodes.source_note: The source explicitly names W_{f,phi} as the space of degenerate Whittaker forms; the extracted Hom formula is OCR-degraded.
candidate_nodes.statement: For a smooth representation (pi,W) and degenerate Whittaker setup (f,phi), W is said to admit a degenerate Whittaker model relative to (f,phi) if W_{U'',theta_f} is nonzero. The space W_{f,phi} of degenerate Whittaker forms on W relative to (f,phi) is defined by W_{U'',theta_f} when U = U'', and, when U != U'', by a Hom-space from the irreducible representation of the Heisenberg quotient U/(U'' intersection ker theta_f) with central character theta_f into W_{U'',theta_f}.

candidate_nodes.label: def:whittaker_orbit_sets
candidate_nodes.remark: The source notation for these two sets is OCR-noisy; likely notation should be confirmed visually before using canonical symbols.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Combines the closure order paragraph with the later definitions of the two orbit sets.
candidate_nodes.statement: Order nilpotent orbits by closure: O < O' means O is contained in the usual-topology closure of O'. For a representation pi with local character coefficients c_O, the paper introduces one set of nilpotent orbits O with c_O != 0 and a second set of nilpotent orbits containing an element f for which there exists a one-parameter subgroup phi satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f and W_{f,phi} != 0.

candidate_nodes.label: ext:harish_chandra_local_character_expansion
candidate_nodes.remark: The span attributes this recalled statement to Harish-Chandra, cited as [Hch].
candidate_nodes.source_note: Source formula (*) is OCR-degraded but the prose identifies the nilpotent orbital Fourier expansion and coefficients c_O.
candidate_nodes.statement: For a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) of G, there is a neighborhood of 1 in G identified by logarithm with a neighborhood of 0 in g on which the distribution character of pi has an expansion as a sum over nilpotent orbits O in g: tr pi = sum_O c_O times the Fourier transform of a suitably normalized invariant measure on O, with Fourier transform taken relative to psi composed with tr.

candidate_nodes.label: ext:rodier_whittaker_model_criterion
candidate_nodes.remark: The formula defining f from theta is not safely legible in the OCR and should be manually transcribed.
candidate_nodes.source_note: The span states this as Rodier's result and then gives the closure-order reformulation.
candidate_nodes.statement: Assume G is split. Let N be a maximal unipotent subgroup of G, T a torus normalizing N, and theta a nondegenerate character of N, meaning its stabilizer in T is the center of G. For the nilpotent orbit O containing the element f associated to theta by the source's pairing formula, a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) admits a Whittaker model relative to theta if and only if c_O != 0. The source also reformulates this as existence of a maximal nilpotent orbit with nonzero coefficient.

candidate_nodes.label: ext:moeglin_waldspurger_main_theorem
candidate_nodes.remark: The equality line continues across two spans; the word completing the condition on phi appears at the start of the following span.
candidate_nodes.source_note: This is presented in the introduction as the principal result of the work and object of Chapter I.
candidate_nodes.statement: The main result of Chapter I says that the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by c_O != 0 coincide with the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by existence of nonzero W_{f,phi}. If O is a maximal element of either set, then c_O = dim W_{f,phi}, where f lies in O and phi is any one-parameter subgroup satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f.

The formula defining the nilpotent element f attached to the nondegenerate character theta is not safely legible in OCR, especially the cases on Lie(N) and the opposite Borel algebra.
The definition of W_{f,phi} contains a damaged displayed line and OCR reads the Hom expression unclearly; the exact group acting on the Hom-space should be checked visually.

The spans cite [Hch], [R1], [B], [13], [R2], [Z], Barbasch-Vogan, and Joseph without bibliography spans; verifier should identify these before admitting external theorem candidates or existence claims.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:article_metadata
notation_contexts.statement: C. Moeglin and J.-L. Waldspurger, Modeles de Whittaker degeneres pour des groupes p-adiques, Math. Z. 196 (1987), 427-452.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:mw_intro_notation
notation_contexts.statement: Use F for a p-adic field of residual characteristic not 2, G for a reductive algebraic group over F, g for its Lie algebra, psi for the fixed continuous character F -> C^*, tr for the chosen nondegenerate G-invariant symmetric bilinear form, and c_O for the nilpotent-orbit coefficients in the local character expansion.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:ocr_normalization
notation_contexts.statement: French OCR is noisy; normalized notation below uses O for a nilpotent orbit, phi for a one-parameter subgroup, theta_f for the character gamma |-> psi(tr(f log gamma)), and W_{f,phi} for the degenerate Whittaker-forms space.

payload.summary: Proposed six conservative source-backed candidates: three definitions for degenerate Whittaker setup, degenerate Whittaker forms, and the two orbit sets; and three external theorem statements covering Harish-Chandra's local character expansion, Rodier's Whittaker criterion, and the Moeglin-Waldspurger main theorem. OCR-heavy formulas were flagged for manual transcription.
